sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2013/2015/2017. Kathu field word lists and audio recordings (Anwang, Balong, Nabi), and Mondzish lexical database (m.s.), Zenodo.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only modern first-hand data on Kathu and Thou (tone-marked ~150-word lists, WAV audio); could reveal prominence patterns in polysyllables even if no prose statement on stress exists.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2014. Mondzish: a new subgroup of Lolo-Burmese. Proceedings of the 14th International Symposium on Chinese Languages and Linguistics (IsCLL-14), Academia Sinica, Taipei, 63-76.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Section 2.1 Kathu, Thou (pp. 65-66): onset clusters /kl- khl- pl- phl-/, tone-numbered forms (ka33 thu33, thou53); characterises Wu Zili 1994 as a brief sketch 'with no more than a few dozen words'; Hsiu's own 2013 word lists (~150 words) are the other Kathu data.

sources.citation: Namkung, Ju (ed.). 1996. Phonological Inventories of Tibeto-Burman Languages. STEDT Monograph Series 3. Berkeley: Center for Southeast Asia Studies. Entry GASU, pp. 108-109 (inventory extracted from Wu Zili 1994, pp. 39-41).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gives Wu 1994's Gasu (Balong) inventory: initials incl. clusters pl/bl/kl/gl/ngl, constricted vs unconstricted vowels, and four tones 'ma55 ma33 ma13 ma31' with notes '/55/ is pronounced closer to [44]' and 'in syllables with constricted vowels, tones /13/ and /31/ become [35] and [51]'. Namkung does include STRESS/ACCENT subsections for other languages where the source has one; the Gasu entry has none.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page kath1251 and reference records 131684 (Wu 1994) and 478595 (Wu 2004); Hammarström hh.bib entries s:Wu:Gasu, hld:Namkung:Tibeto-Burman, hld:ShearerHongkai:China, hel:Bradley:EAsia.
sources.note: Only two descriptive refs (both Wu Zili). hh.bib additionally lists Gasu among the languages covered by Namkung 1996, Shearer & Sun 2017 (Yi-SE-Gasu) and Bradley 2007; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: CASS ncpssd.cn search API (title/keyword/author searches for 嘎苏, 嘎苏话, 嘎苏语, 广南+彝, Kathu, 武自立) and Google Books feed searches (嘎苏话, 嘎僳话, 云南特殊语言研究).
sources.note: No further phonological description of Kathu exists in these indexes. Other hits: Wang Ting & He Yingdong 2020, 彝汉杂居村彝族语言使用状况调查——以云南省广南县南屏镇大牙扫村彝族为例 (文教资料; sociolinguistic use survey of a Kathu village, no phonology); Li Yunbing 2008 中国南方民族语言语序类型研究 / 2025 The Word Order Typology of Minority Languages in Southern China (cite 嘎苏话 word-order data only).

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. Kathu page, Languages of Mainland Southeast Asia site (sites.google.com/site/msealangs/mondzish-branch/kathu) and publications page.
sources.note: Village locations (Anwang, Balong, Dayashao, Laojing villages), informants, tone-marked autonyms; points to Zenodo audio (2013, 2015) and the Mondzish lexical database (zenodo.org/record/1249169) — zenodo.org could not be reached by automated download for every request by automated download. Nothing on stress.

sources.note: Onset clusters and tone-numbered forms from Wu 2004 only; no statement on stress. References are Wu 1994, Wu 2004, Hsiu 2014, Bradley 1997/2007, Pelkey 2011.

sources.note: Primary phonology (pp. 39-41: initials, finals, four tones) + lexicon and grammar notes; the only place a first-hand remark on stress or on tone/prominence in polysyllables could exist. Full text (PDF 506 kB) is on ncpssd.cn behind a free-registration login (Chinese phone number needed) and on CNKI (MZYW402.006).
